title: Check your understanding: Verifying the Git Installation

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of verifying the git installation?
options: Git must be installed and reachable from the terminal before repository commands can work. Version and help output establish which command behavior your environment supports.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Git must be installed and reachable from the terminal before repository commands can work. Version and help output establish which command behavior your environment supports.
questions.explanation: Git must be installed and reachable from the terminal before repository commands can work. Version and help output establish which command behavior your environment supports.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git --version` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with verifying the git installation?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
